subject: AcmeOps: credit proration and ERP sync for pilot conversion
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeops.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@acmeops.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Credit proration for pilot conversion + ERP sync

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the help during our pilot. We’re ready to convert to a paid subscription as of 2027-07-15 but noticed the invoice generated for July included the full month instead of prorated days. Can Redwood apply a proration credit for the 16-day half-month and send us either (A) a credit memo we can apply in NetSuite or (B) instructions for an invoice offset so our AP team can reconcile?

I attached our usage export for the pilot window so you can see the billing dates. Happy to loop in our AP contact if you need an official PO or billing contact.

Attachments: initial-usage-report.csv (CSV, ~12KB)

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jordan

Jordan Lee
Finance Ops | AcmeOps
[jordan.lee@acmeops.com]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeops.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Credit proration for pilot conversion + ERP sync

Jordan — thanks for the dataset and flag. I think we can do a formal credit memo for the prorated period and have Finance either post it to NetSuite or provide a one-line invoice offset, depending on what your ERP team prefers.

Next steps I propose:
- Finance (Marcus / Neha) confirms the G/L mapping and whether we should issue a credit memo vs invoice offset.
- If credit memo: Finance will draft the memo and send a PDF and NetSuite memo ID for your AP to accept and apply.
- If offset: we’ll create an internal billing ticket and include the offset account and memo so your AR can net it on the next invoice.

Can Marcus/Neha weigh in on the accounting treatment and timing? Jordan — if you can tell us whether AcmeOps prefers credit memos in NetSuite or invoice offsets, that will speed things up.

Thanks — I’ll hold on processing until Finance confirms.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Credit proration for pilot conversion + ERP sync

Per internal review: we’re fine issuing a credit memo for the prorated amount. A couple of accounting details to confirm before we generate the PDF:

1) G/L mapping — recommend posting to 4400 (Contractual Allowances / Revenue Contra) so the revenue deferral rolls correctly. If legal/GAAP would prefer a different contra account for pilot credits, flag now.
2) Tax treatment — the credit is for service usage; confirm whether AcmeOps requires a tax-adjusted memo (Jordan?).
3) Application method — we can either:
   a) Create a credit memo in NetSuite and provide the memo number for your AP to apply; or
   b) Issue an internal invoice offset that will reduce the upcoming Aug invoice by the credit amount (no external memo object).

Operational note: Option (a) gives AcmeOps a clear artifact inside NetSuite which is often preferred by enterprise AP teams. Option (b) is faster if we can coordinate before the next billing run (cutoff is 2027-08-10).

If we go with (a) we’ll need: PO number (if required), a NetSuite customer ID (or the tenant ID we already have), and confirmation on tax. If (b), Vanessa — please confirm we have authorization to adjust the Aug invoice pre-billing.

I’ll prepare a draft credit-memo PDF for Vanessa to share with Jordan once we confirm method.

— Marcus Lin
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeops.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Credit proration for pilot conversion + ERP sync

Jordan / Vanessa / Marcus —

Thanks for the clarifications. AcmeOps confirmed they prefer an on-ledger credit memo in NetSuite so their AP can apply it against the July invoice. Jordan flagged that their tax code is standard US sales/service tax — no special treatment. PO number is PO-8675309 and customer NetSuite ID is NS-ACME-0042 (provided by Jordan in a side message).

We’ll proceed with option (a): create and post a credit memo in NetSuite, then share the memo PDF and the NetSuite memo ID with AcmeOps. Draft actions and postings: 
- Draft credit memo amount: $1,240.00 (proration for 2027-07-16 — 2027-07-31).
- Posting G/L: 4400 (Revenue Contra).
- Reference: Deal D-2027-0042 / PO-8675309.
- Tax: no adjustment required.

I attached the draft credit memo for review. I’ll post the memo in NetSuite this afternoon and link the memo number here once posted. Please confirm final wording and we’ll send the PDF to Jordan and AP.

Attachments: credit-memo-draft.pdf (PDF, ~7KB)

— Neha Kapoor
Senior Accountant, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | Finance & Billing
